summary.text: 西 is the character for “west.” A traditional analysis treats the whole graph as a bird’s nest and links the westward direction to birds roosting at sunset, but both that pictorial account and the proposed route to “west” remain disputed.

formation.text: The proposed nest analysis is pictographic: it reads the whole graph as a bird’s nest, without dividing it into modern-looking parts. Another proposal attributes a different early form to a borrowing from 囟 because of sound similarity. Accounts differ on whether the directional word was written by reusing the nest graph for a similar-sounding word or whether “west” developed through the sunset-and-roosting association; neither sequence is settled.

components.text: The whole graph is interpreted in one account as a bird’s nest. This is a disputed pictorial analysis; it does not establish the object’s name or prove how the graph came to mean “west.”

history.text: Graphic records identify oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and small-seal stages, but do not establish a detailed sequence of stroke changes. The curated seal-script image is a modern vector reconstruction, not a dated artifact, and its form does not resolve the origin dispute.
A separate proposal holds that one early form borrowed 囟 because the ancient words sounded similar, and that the form later developed into 西. This proposed graphic history remains unsettled.

uncertainties.text: The nest interpretation, the proposal involving 囟, and the bag-or-basket account are competing explanations; the evidence here does not settle the origin. For the nest account, it is also unresolved whether “west” was written by sound-based borrowing or arose through the sunset association.
No supported name or pronunciation for a depicted nest, bag, or basket is available to establish that the directional word was borrowed on the basis of that object’s name.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions; precise dates unresolved
senses.text: 西 is reported for the western direction in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions. No individually dated examples establish a precise first use.

senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions; precise dates unresolved
senses.text: The graph is also reported in place and palace names in these inscriptional periods. Their order relative to the directional use is unresolved.

“Nest” is proposed as the referent of the pictographic analysis, and one graphic-history account describes it as an original meaning no longer in use. This is not established as the earliest attested single-character use.

limitations.text: The accounts do not establish whether the western-direction use arose by borrowing the graph for a similar-sounding word or through a semantic association with sunset and roosting. No individually dated examples establish the sequence.

overview.text: 西 means “west.” One disputed interpretation sees the whole graph as a bird’s nest and explains “west” through birds roosting at sunset; another proposes that the graph was reused for a similar-sounding directional word.

components.text: One interpretation reads the whole graph as a bird’s nest; this is disputed, and the route from that picture to “west” is unresolved.
